verdictSummary: Scrivener's solo core is compact: build a local-first long-form authoring app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on polish, sync, importers.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local-first long-form authoring app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
whyPeopleStillPay: Scrivener: People pay for a writing surface they trust for years, plus migration tools, sync, and tiny interaction details that disappear into habit.
ongoingBurden: Own schema migrations, backups, sync conflicts, export compatibility, and long-term file readability.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Local-first open-source workspace with documents and databases.

priorArt.name: Logseq
priorArt.desc: Open-source local knowledge graph and outliner.

alternatives.name: Kindling
alternatives.desc: A tiny new Scrivener-shaped app that imports the real thing and keeps the outline beside the draft.

facts.install: Native macOS DMG, Windows MSI, or Linux AppImage/.deb
facts.dataFormat: Each writing project is a local SQLite file; Kindling works offline and does not upload manuscripts, account data, analytics, or telemetry
facts.gapVsPaid: It is young and intentionally small, so it lacks Scrivener's mature research binder, corkboard, metadata, snapshots, targets and highly configurable Compile system.

alternatives.name: Manuskript
alternatives.desc: Scrivener's broad outline, rebuilt by volunteers and left with rougher edges.

facts.install: Windows portable ZIP, Linux .deb/.rpm/Flatpak/Snap, or source install on macOS
facts.dataFormat: Projects save on local disk in Manuskript's open plain-text project format; the default single-file project is an archive, with an uncompressed-folder mode also available
facts.gapVsPaid: It imitates much of Scrivener's structure but is rougher and less reliable around editing polish, project stability and professional compile/export workflows.
facts.setupBlocker: Windows antivirus may flag the unsigned PyInstaller build; macOS has no current packaged app and requires running from source, while DOCX/EPUB export needs Pandoc

alternatives.name: novelWriter
alternatives.desc: A manuscript binder made of plain text, with fewer knobs than Scrivener.

facts.install: Signed Windows installer or Linux AppImage/.deb; macOS currently requires pipx/PyPI
facts.dataFormat: A project is a normal local directory containing many human-readable plain-text documents plus project metadata and configuration files
facts.gapVsPaid: Its plain-text, fiction-focused project model is more portable but offers a narrower research binder and far less configurable formatting and compilation than Scrivener.
facts.setupBlocker: As of release 2026.1 there is no macOS DMG, so Mac users must create a Python environment and install the package

rejectedAlternatives.name: Story Architect
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Real installers and active work, but the project still calls the current release beta.

notes: Strong page because Scrivener separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Scrivener.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local-first long-form authoring app with fast capture, full-text search, backlinks, tags, and Markdown export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: conflict-safe multi-device sync; mature importers and exporters; collaborative editing and sharing.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
